parts.label: whole
parts.given_text: On reaching the rough surface, the speed satisfies v² = 2gh. The constant deceleration needed to stop in distance d is a = v²/(2d).

parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A ball of mass m strikes a vertical wall horizontally at speed u and rebounds in the opposite direction at speed v. The collision lasts time T. Determine the magnitude of the average force exerted by the wall.

answer.text: The momentum change has magnitude m(u + v), so the average force is m(u + v)/T.

ibd-a4aeacaa02d5bc2c-q7:whole.hint: Isolate the named object. Add an arrow for each interaction it has with its surroundings.
notes: Draw only forces acting on this object: weight, contact force, tension, friction or other stated interactions. Label directions and place weight at the centre of mass.
The resultant is the vector sum of these forces. Do not add an extra “ma force” or put a Newton’s-third-law reaction on the same object.

ibd-a4aeacaa02d5bc2c-q9:whole.hint: Choose a system containing the interacting objects and compare its total momentum before and after the event.
notes: When external impulse is negligible, Σmu = Σmv. Keep velocity signs, and apply the equation separately in each direction for a two-dimensional collision.
“Sticks together” gives one shared final velocity. Kinetic energy is conserved only for an elastic collision; momentum conservation alone does not make a collision elastic.

ibd-a4aeacaa02d5bc2c-q23:whole.hint: Draw a force equation for each connected body, using compatible positive directions along the string.
notes: An inextensible taut string links the accelerations. A light string over an ideal pulley has the same tension on both sides.
To find acceleration, combine the equations to eliminate internal tension. Then substitute back into a single-body equation to find the tension.

ibd-b9b4616ad701fc8d-q1:whole.hint: Choose the object or system and identify the resultant force, rather than using one force on its own.
notes: Newton’s second law is ΣF = ma. Resolve into independent directions; zero acceleration requires zero resultant force in that direction.
Newton’s third-law forces act on different bodies and are the same kind of interaction. Balanced forces act on the same body.

duplicate-c106258d8d056ecc.hint: Sketch the initial and final vectors. A change is final minus initial, with the arrows still carrying direction.
notes: Calculate changes component by component: Δv = v_final − v_initial, or Δp = p_final − p_initial. Reversing direction requires a sign change.
An unchanged speed does not mean unchanged velocity. State both magnitude and direction when a vector is requested.

ibd-b9b4616ad701fc8d-q5:whole.hint: Compare the upward resistive force with the weight at each stage, rather than assuming the acceleration stays constant.
notes: Use resultant force = ma with a declared positive direction. Drag increases with speed in the stated model, while weight is essentially constant.
Terminal speed means balanced forces and zero acceleration; it does not mean zero speed. Opening a parachute can reverse the direction of acceleration before the motion reverses.

duplicate-c0e5b18106fbcff6.hint: Consider the momentum carried away or brought in by the mass flowing each second.
notes: Force is the rate of momentum change. For a stream brought to rest, its magnitude is mass flow rate multiplied by the change in velocity.
For density ρ, area A and speed v, mass flow rate is ρAv. Include direction and any incoming momentum when applying the relation to a nozzle or rocket.

ibd-b9b4616ad701fc8d-q9:whole.hint: Choose the object or system and identify the resultant force, rather than using one force on its own.
notes: Newton’s second law is ΣF = ma. Resolve into independent directions; zero acceleration requires zero resultant force in that direction.
Newton’s third-law forces act on different bodies and are the same kind of interaction. Balanced forces act on the same body.

ibd-b9b4616ad701fc8d-q19:whole.hint: Mark the centre of the circle. Which components of the real forces point towards it?
notes: Use ΣF_radial = mv²/r towards the centre. “Centripetal force” names this resultant; it is not an additional force.
At the top and bottom of a vertical circle the weight contributes with different radial signs. At loss of contact or a just-taut string, set the contact force or tension to zero.

ibd-83f224ae8d628d0e-q5:whole.hint: Resolve forces parallel and perpendicular to the contact surface. Decide which way the object would tend to move.
notes: For a simple incline, weight has components mg sin θ down the plane and mg cos θ into it. Other applied forces can change the normal reaction.
Kinetic friction has magnitude μ_k N. Static friction adjusts up to μ_s N; use the maximum only at impending slip, and choose its direction to oppose relative slipping.

duplicate-fce2262e7d0d4352.hint: Express one complete turn in radians and identify the time for that turn.
notes: Angular speed is ω = 2π/T; linear speed at radius r is v = ωr.
Convert the period to seconds before quoting rad s⁻¹. Angular speed and linear speed are different quantities.

duplicate-93b29ee7fb80a950.hint: Write the required quantity in terms of the measurements, then track how each measurement’s uncertainty contributes.
notes: For products and quotients, add fractional uncertainties; for powers, multiply fractional uncertainty by the magnitude of the power. For sums and differences, combine absolute uncertainties using the stated worst-case convention.
For a graph gradient, use the steepest and shallowest acceptable lines through the error bars. Report an uncertainty with matching precision to the quantity, not extra calculator digits.
